--- first prompt (stdin) ---
We are working through the plan in @docs/PLAN.md, unattended, on branch `main`.
Read CLAUDE.md (if the repo has one) and @docs/PLAN.md in full before touching anything. The plan
says what to build, in what order, and how a milestone is verified and recorded. Then read the
**last entry only** of `docs/PLAN.progress.md`, the progress log (it may not exist yet). Where the plan
or the repo's own instructions are more specific than this prompt, follow them.

Implement the next milestone (or task) in the plan that is not done yet, verify it, tick it in
the plan, log it in `docs/PLAN.progress.md`, and commit it. By the plan's checklist the next open item is `2. Scripts. Write the scripts.`. Confirm that against the plan's own ordering and dependencies. 

Any design question that would normally go to the user, you decide autonomously, the way the
plan's existing decisions point. Record each such decision in docs/PLAN.md.

---

## Loop protocol

You are one link in an unattended chain. A driver script (`plan_loop.py`)
started this session and will start others after it. Nothing carries between sessions except
what is on disk, so `docs/PLAN.md` and `docs/PLAN.progress.md` are not documentation of your work: they *are*
the handoff. A milestone you land but do not write up is a milestone the next session redoes.

**One milestone per turn.** Do exactly one milestone, then end your turn with the
`LOOP_STATUS` line below. Do not start a second one in the same turn, even if the first went
quickly. After your turn the driver measures this session's context: under 30% it sends
you the next milestone in this same session, otherwise it ends the session and a fresh one
continues. That is the driver's decision, not yours.

**Start by checking the working tree.** Run `git status` and `git log --oneline -5`. If the
tree is dirty, a previous session was cut off mid-milestone (usage limit, timeout, crash). Read
the diff and that milestone's entry in `docs/PLAN.progress.md` if it has one, decide whether the work is
sound, and finish it or revert it deliberately. Never commit it blindly.

**Two files, two jobs.** Every session reads the whole plan, so the plan must stay the size of
the work still ahead, not grow with the work behind.
- `docs/PLAN.md` holds what a *later* milestone needs: the spec, the checklist, the decisions
  taken, verified facts, blockers. When you tick a milestone, its checklist line gets at most
  one sentence saying what landed and the subject line of its commit. Nothing else about the
  past goes into the plan: no evidence, no command output, no narrative.
- `docs/PLAN.progress.md` holds the *past*: one entry per milestone, appended at the end, never edited
  later. Create the file with your entry if it does not exist. Each entry has this shape, so
  the next session can find it with the milestone's name:

      ## <YYYY-MM-DD> <milestone label as it appears in the plan>
      Commit: <the commit's subject line>
      Delivered: <what exists now that did not before>
      Verified: <the gate, the command, what you observed>
      Open: <what is not done, what you ruled out and why, or "nothing">

  Read it selectively: the last entry at the start of a session, and the entry of a specific
  milestone only when the tree is dirty or the milestone you take was left `PARTIAL` or
  blocked. Never read it in full.
- If the plan still carries history paragraphs written before this rule, move them into
  `docs/PLAN.progress.md` as you come across them, a few at a time in the same commit as your
  milestone. Never make that a milestone of its own.

**Scope.** Take the first milestone that is not done, honouring the dependencies the plan
names. Do not silently substitute a different one: if it is genuinely blocked (it needs a human,
a missing tool, a decision only the owner can make), mark it blocked in the plan naming the
blocker, take the next unblocked one, and name the swap in your `LOOP_STATUS` line.

**Branch.** Stay on `main`. Never push, merge, rebase, switch branches or rewrite
existing commits.

**Commits.** The owner has asked, once and for the whole chain, for every completed and
verified milestone to be committed. That standing instruction overrides any "commit only when
asked" rule in the repo. Use the commit message convention the repo documents. Never skip hooks
or bypass signing. If a commit fails on signing or a hook you cannot fix, leave the work staged,
put a dated `COMMIT PENDING` note on the milestone in the plan, and report it.

**Definition of done.** All of these, or it is not landed:
1. Implemented, after re-reading the milestone's section against the current source. Fix the
   plan if a fact in it has drifted.
2. Builds, and its tests pass, using the commands the plan and CLAUDE.md give.
3. Verified against the milestone's own gate, with evidence you actually observed: command
   output, readbacks, log lines. Never mark a milestone done on reasoning alone.
4. The plan updated: the milestone ticked with its one-line summary, any new verified facts in
   the section the plan keeps for them, and any autonomous decision with the date and a
   one-line reason.
5. The progress log `docs/PLAN.progress.md` extended with the milestone's entry, in the shape above.
6. Every other doc the repo says must track the change updated in the same commit.
7. Committed.

**Honest over optimistic.** If you cannot land it, leave the plan saying exactly what is done,
what is open and what you ruled out. Commit whatever is safe to commit. A wrong "done" costs the
next session far more than an honest "in progress".

**Gates you cannot self-certify.** If a gate is a human judgement ("feels right", "looks
good"), do the measurable half, record it, and say plainly that a human pass is required. Never
rate your own work against a subjective bar and call it passed.

**Leave the environment usable.** The next session needs the same machine. Stop the processes
you started unless the plan expects them running, leave no modal dialog or blocking prompt
open, and leave any app the plan's dev loop relies on in the state the plan describes.

**Spend context carefully.** A long session is cut at a milestone checkpoint once it is
30% full. Read files in the slices you need, and hand broad searches and big readings to
subagents so that only their conclusions enter your context.

**Improve the tooling as you go.** If an instruction in CLAUDE.md, the plan or the docs misled
you, fix it in the same commit. That is how the chain gets better instead of repeating itself.

**Final message.** One short paragraph of what happened, including any autonomous decision
and where you recorded it. Then a final line that is *exactly* one of these, which the driver
reads:

    LOOP_STATUS: LANDED <milestone>
    LOOP_STATUS: PARTIAL <milestone> — <one-line reason>
    LOOP_STATUS: BLOCKED — <one-line reason>
    LOOP_STATUS: PLAN_COMPLETE

Use `PLAN_COMPLETE` only when no milestone in scope is left open. Use `BLOCKED` only when no
open milestone in scope can be taken without a human: the driver stops the chain on it and
waits for the owner.


--- continue prompt (stdin), shown at 12% context ---
Milestone checkpoint passed. This session's context is 12.0% full, under the
30% rotation threshold, so the driver has kept you in the same session for the next
milestone.

Do not re-read the plan in full: you read it this session, and the checklist as the driver reads
it from docs/PLAN.md right now is:

- [x] 1. Done already. Nothing to do.
- [ ] 2. Scripts. Write the scripts.
- [ ] 3. Build. Build it.

Confirm with `git status` that the tree is clean, then take the next milestone that is not done
and read only its section of the plan. By the plan's checklist the next open item is `2. Scripts. Write the scripts.`. Confirm that against the plan's own ordering and dependencies. 

Same loop protocol as before: exactly one milestone this turn, the same definition of done, the
plan ticked with one line, the entry appended to `docs/PLAN.progress.md`, commit it, and end with the
`LOOP_STATUS` line.
